introduction: On this fourth Sunday of Advent, Micah announces that a ruler will come from little Bethlehem, and he will be our peace. In the Gospel, Mary hurries to visit Elizabeth, and the child in Elizabeth's womb leaps for joy. The Letter to the Hebrews tells us that Christ came into the world saying, I have come to do your will. Christmas is very near. Let us welcome the Lord with Mary's faith.

prayerOfTheFaithful.invitation: Brothers and sisters, blessed is she who believed. With Mary, let us bring our prayers to the Father.
intentions: For the Church: that, like Mary, she may carry Christ to everyone she meets. Let us pray to the Lord.
For expectant mothers and their unborn children: that they may be protected, welcomed and loved. Let us pray to the Lord.
For those who are lonely at this time of year: that someone may visit them and bring them joy. Let us pray to the Lord.
For peace in the world: that the one born in Bethlehem may be our peace. Let us pray to the Lord.
For ourselves: that we may believe God's word as Mary did, and do his will. Let us pray to the Lord.
prayerOfTheFaithful.conclusion: Lord God, you chose the Virgin Mary to bear your Son. Give us her faith and her haste to serve, so that we may welcome Christ with joy at Christmas. Through Christ our Lord.

reflection.title: Blessed is she who believed
reflection.body:
The prophet Micah turns our eyes to a small, insignificant town: "But you, Bethlehem Ephrathah, being small among the clans of Judah, out of you one will come out to me who is to be ruler in Israel." God chooses what is small. And the ruler who comes will shepherd his people "in the strength of the LORD," and "He will be our peace."

In the Gospel, Mary has just received the angel's message. She does not stay at home to think about her own news. She sets out "with haste" to visit her elderly cousin Elizabeth, who is also expecting a child. Love does not wait.

When Mary greets her, something remarkable happens: "When Elizabeth heard Mary's greeting, the baby leaped in her womb." The unborn John recognizes the unborn Jesus. Elizabeth, filled with the Holy Spirit, cries out, "Blessed are you among women, and blessed is the fruit of your womb!" and asks in wonder, "Why am I so favored, that the mother of my Lord should come to me?" Then she praises Mary's faith: "Blessed is she who believed, for there will be a fulfillment of the things which have been spoken to her from the Lord!"

The Letter to the Hebrews shows us the heart of the Son who is coming. When he comes into the world, he says, "Behold, I have come to do your will." Mary's yes and the Son's yes meet in this mystery.

With Christmas only days away, there is much to do. But Mary shows us what matters most: faith in God's word and love that hurries to serve. This week, visit someone who needs company, as Mary visited Elizabeth. And in the rush of preparations, find a quiet moment to say to God, as Mary did, let it be done to me.
